title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended to be the canonical reference for People Ops, Finance, Security, and Engineering teams.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, interns, and vendors with Redwood accounts or network access.
- Covers corporate systems (SSO, G Suite/Workspace, Okta), production and non-production cloud accounts, corporate finance systems (Expensify/Billing), and vendor onboarding.

Owners and Review Cadence
- Policy owner: People Ops (primary)
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (co-owner for access/data controls)
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal (co-owner for procurement/vendor policy)
- Review cadence: annual full review and ad-hoc updates after material events (breaches, regulatory requirements, org changes).

1) Access and permissions
Purpose: Limit access to systems and data using least privilege, documented approvals, and periodic review.
Key concepts:
- Role-based access: Use defined roles (employee, contractor, admin, SRE, dev-prod-access) mapped to minimal permissions.
- Just-in-time (JIT) access: Privileged access granted temporarily via approval workflow for critical systems.
- Separation of duties: No single user should have both change approval and change deployment rights for production services.

Standard process:
1. Access request: Submit via internal Access Request form (Okta self-service link). Include justification, duration, and approver.
2. Manager approval: Direct manager approves initial request.
3. Resource owner approval: Service owner (listed in infra atlas) must approve role assignment for production resources.
4. Provisioning: IT/Cloud infra team performs provisioning through infrastructure-as-code or RBAC console.
5. Review: Quarterly access review by team leads; privileged access review every 90 days.

Required controls:
- SSO enforced for all corporate services (Okta).
- MFA required for all accounts, hardware MFA for privileged roles.
- Logging enabled for privilege elevation and admin actions.
- Deprovisioning must occur within 24 hours of termination or role change (People Ops trigger).

2) Change management
Purpose: Ensure safe, auditable changes to production and shared services while minimizing downtime and risk.
Applicability: All changes to production infra, runtime, databases, and customer-impacting services.

Change categories:
- Standard change: Low-risk, pre-approved changes with runbook (e.g., routine config updates).
- Minor change: Low to medium risk; requires change request and peer review.
- Major change: High-risk changes (schema migrations, release window changes) require RFC, scheduled maintenance window, and pre/post validation.

Process (high level):
1. Create Change Request (CR) in ServiceNow/JIRA: include rollback plan, test plan, blast radius, owners, and communication plan.
2. Review & Approval: CR review by service owner, SRE on-call, and security if applicable. Major changes require CAB approval.
3. Scheduling: Schedule in change calendar during approved windows; publish maintenance notice to status page.
4. Execution: Follow runbook, use feature flags/canary where appropriate, monitor metrics and logs.
5. Post-change validation: Run acceptance checklist, confirm SLOs and alerts are healthy.
6. Postmortem: For any incident or unexpected behavior, create a postmortem within 72 hours.

Key thresholds and SLAs:
- Emergency changes: Allowed only with Operational Lead + Engineering Manager approval; must be documented retroactively within 24 hours.
- Rollback target: If critical SLOs degrade >5% within 30 minutes, initiate rollback.

3) Data management
Purpose: Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while enabling product development.
Data classification:
- Public: Information intended for public consumption (marketing pages, blog posts).
- Internal: Non-sensitive internal docs and operational data.
- Confidential: Customer data, contracts, non-public financials, PII.

Retention & lifecycle:
- Default retention: 7 years for financial/audit records; 2 years for most operational logs unless required for investigations.
- Shorter-lived datasets (dev/test): Purge after 90 days unless explicitly retained.
- Backups: Production customer data backed up daily; backups tested quarterly.

Access & handling:
- Confidential data requires RBAC controls, encryption at rest and in transit, and strict logging/audit trails.
- Use approved storage locations only (cloud accounts managed by eng-infra).
- Data sharing: Must be approved by Data Steward and recorded in the data catalog.

Incident & breach response:
- Report suspected data exfiltration to Security immediately via incident channel.
- Follow Incident Response runbook: containment, eradication, recovery, and notification.

4) Procurement and expenses
Purpose: Provide clear, auditable procedures for purchasing, vendor contracting, corporate cards, and expense reimbursement.
Procurement thresholds & approvals:
- Purchases < $5,000: Manager approval required.
- Purchases $5,000 to $50,000: Manager + Finance approval required.
- Purchases > $50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal approval and sourcing evaluation.

Corporate card & expense policy:
- Corporate card issuance: Controller approval and manager sign-off.
- Personal card reimbursements: Submit receipts in Expensify within 30 days.
- Per diem & travel allowances: Use travel policy below. Non-compliant expenses may be denied.

Procurement process:
1. Initiation: Submit Purchase Request in Procurement portal with justification and budget code.
2. Sourcing: Purchasing team obtains quotes for purchases > $10,000.
3. Purchase order (PO): Finance issues PO; vendor may not begin work without PO/contract.
4. Receipt & payment: Verify invoices against PO; Finance processes payment net 30 unless otherwise negotiated.

5) Vendor management
Purpose: Standardize onboarding, contracting, risk assessment, and offboarding of third-party vendors.
Vendor risk tiers:
- Low: SaaS tools with no access to confidential data (e.g., marketing tools).
- Medium: Services with limited access to internal systems or non-sensitive data.
- High: Vendors with access to production systems, customer data, or that host critical services.

Onboarding checklist:
1. Risk assessment: Security team completes vendor security questionnaire and assigns risk tier.
2. Contract review: Legal reviews contract for data processing addendums (DPAs) and SLAs.
3. Provisioning: Limit access per least privilege; use vendor-specific service accounts and rotate credentials.
4. Monitoring: Configure logging/alerts for vendor activity where applicable.
5. Renewal & review: Annual vendor review and performance evaluation for high-risk vendors.

Termination & offboarding:
- Revoke access immediately upon contract termination.
- Ensure data deletion/return per contract and maintain evidence of completion.

6) Travel policy
Purpose: Ensure safe, cost-effective, and auditable travel for business needs.
Booking & approvals:
- All travel must be pre-approved by the employee's manager.
- Use the company travel portal or approved booking tool to get preferred rates and travel insurance.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business class requires Director-level approval for flights >6 hours.

Reimbursable expenses:
- Airfare, lodging, ground transportation (Uber/Taxi/Train), meals (subject to per diem), and necessary business-related incidentals.
- Alcohol allowed in moderation and reimbursed when part of a business meal with client/partner.

Per diem & limits:
- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals and incidental expenses when receipts not provided.
- International per diem: Rates vary by country; consult Finance published table.

Safety & emergency:
- Travel insurance is provided for all international trips.
- Employees must register international travel with People Ops for emergency notifications.

7) Internal templates and artifacts
This section centralizes links to commonly used templates. Templates are maintained in the Templates workspace and must be used for compliance and traceability.
- Purchase Request template: /confluence/templates/purchase-request (use for all procurements)
- Vendor Security questionnaire: /confluence/templates/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Change Request template: /confluence/templates/change-request
- Incident report template: /confluence/templates/incident-report
- Travel request & expense report: /confluence/templates/travel-request

Enforcement and exceptions
- Exceptions must be submitted in writing to People Ops with a business justification and signed by the requestor's manager. Exceptions are time-limited (typically 90 days) and require an owner.
- Non-compliance may result in revocation of privileges, expense denial, or disciplinary action depending on severity.

Frequently referenced contacts
- People Ops (policy questions, exceptions): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Finance (procurement, expense disputes): finance@redwood.ai
- Security (access requests for sensitive systems, incident reporting): secops@redwood.ai
- Procurement mailbox: procurement@redwood.ai
